kbDocuments.title: SOP: High-Pressure Refrigerant & Chiller Safety Lockout
kbDocuments.safety_sop: MANDATORY SAFETY SOP: Before inspecting or servicing any chiller tripping on high discharge pressure (>220 PSI), wear thermal/chemical goggles, insulated gloves, and safety shoes. Verify condenser fan breakers are locked out (LOTO) and confirm zero shaft rotation before removing fan guards. Never vent R-134a refrigerant to atmosphere; use EPA-certified recovery manifold.
kbDocuments.content: High-pressure trips (>230 PSI) on Carrier 30XA screw chillers indicate severely reduced condenser heat rejection. Always apply Lockout-Tagout (LOTO) at the main 480V isolator and individual fan breakers before touching condenser fan blades or electrical junction boxes. Use calibrated manifold gauges rated for R-134a high-side pressures.

kbDocuments.title: Carrier 30XA High Discharge Pressure Troubleshooting Tree
kbDocuments.safety_sop: Isolate main disconnect and apply LOTO before opening condenser fan junction box or touching rotating blades.
kbDocuments.content: Symptom: Circuit A/B High Discharge Pressure (>235 PSI) and intermittent compressor trip. Step 1: Verify all condenser fan banks spin freely and check motor amp draw against 480V nameplate (nominal 3.2A). If fan #1 or #2 is stalled, humming, or tripping thermal overload, inspect dual run capacitor (45uF, CAP-45UF-440V) and motor winding resistance (balanced 3-phase within 5%). Step 2: Check condenser coil fins for fouling or airflow blockage. Step 3: Verify discharge pressure transducer 4-20mA signal matches calibrated manifold gauge.

kbDocuments.title: Carrier 30XA Condenser Fan Motor Replacement Manual (CFM-30XA-480V)
kbDocuments.safety_sop: ELECTRICAL HAZARD (480V 3-Phase): Lock out and tag out 480V main feeder, verify zero voltage phase-to-phase and phase-to-ground with CAT IV multimeter before disconnecting motor leads.
kbDocuments.content: Replacement Procedure for CFM-30XA-480V (or compatible alternate CFM-30XA-ALT-480V): 1. Apply 480V LOTO. 2. Remove top grille assembly and mark fan blade hub height on shaft. 3. Disconnect 3-phase motor whip and ground lug. 4. Torque new motor mount bolts to 18 Nm. 5. Verify clockwise blade rotation on bump test. Temporary Workaround if motor unavailable: Isolate failed circuit on dual-circuit chiller and cap load at 60% while monitoring loop supply temp.

kbDocuments.title: Past Fix Report: CH-07 Recurring Condenser Fan & Capacitor Failures
kbDocuments.safety_sop: Follow roof safety harness rules and LOTO before accessing CH-07 condenser deck.
kbDocuments.content: Historical analysis on Orion Tech Park CH-07: In INC0009715, condenser fan #1 suffered bearing seizure due to monsoon moisture ingress and was replaced with CFM-30XA-480V. In INC0009912 (74 days ago), fan #2 capacitor CAP-45UF-440V failed causing thermal overload. Whenever high discharge pressure recurs on CH-07, inspect both fan #2 motor bearings/windings and capacitor health, and schedule a preventive check on sibling unit CH-08.

kbDocuments.title: SOP: Electrical Lockout-Tagout (LOTO) & Arc Flash PPE
kbDocuments.safety_sop: MANDATORY ELECTRICAL SOP: Wear minimum 8 cal/cm2 arc-rated FR clothing, voltage-rated insulating gloves, and face shield when testing energized 480V or 11kV panels. Test-Before-Touch using live-dead-live multimeter verification.
kbDocuments.content: All field technicians performing work on 480V motors, UPS battery banks, or switchgear must apply personal padlock and danger tag at upstream breaker, record LOTO tag ID in Work Order safety checklist, and obtain supervisor sign-off for live infrared scans.

kbDocuments.title: SOP: R-134a Refrigerant Handling & Leak Testing
kbDocuments.safety_sop: REFRIGERANT SAFETY SOP: Ensure open-air clearance, avoid open flames or hot surfaces (R-134a decomposes to toxic HF gas), wear cryogenic gloves when disconnecting hoses, and use recovery cylinder.
kbDocuments.content: Standard leak check uses dry nitrogen pressure test (max 150 PSI) plus electronic halogen leak detector. Log cylinder serial number and weight delta on any refrigerant top-up.

kbDocuments.title: Vertiv Liebert PEX CRAC Humidity & Airflow Calibration
kbDocuments.safety_sop: Verify raised floor tile stability and wear ESD wrist strap inside Data Hall 1.
kbDocuments.content: If return air humidity drifts above 60% RH, inspect infrared humidifier pan scale, condensate drain trap, and proportional chilled water valve actuator stroke (0-10VDC).

kbDocuments.title: Schneider Galaxy VX UPS Battery Impedance Troubleshooting
kbDocuments.safety_sop: High DC bus voltage (>400VDC) present even with AC input isolated. Use insulated tools only.
kbDocuments.content: Battery string impedance alarms above 15% baseline require individual block voltage and internal ohmic measurement (UPS-BAT-12V9AH). Replace any cell below 11.8V float.

kbDocuments.title: Daikin AHU-D40 Supply Fan Vibration & Belt Alignment Guide
kbDocuments.safety_sop: Lock out VFD drive and wait 5 minutes for DC capacitor bleed-down before opening fan plenum.
kbDocuments.content: Excessive vibration (>4.5 mm/s RMS) is typically caused by worn V-belts, misaligned sheaves, or fouled blower wheel blades. Inspect pillow-block bearing grease lines.

kbDocuments.title: ABB UniGear ZS1 Switchgear Infrared Thermography Standard
kbDocuments.safety_sop: Maintain 1.2m arc flash boundary. Do not open bolted rear busbar covers while energized.
kbDocuments.content: Capture thermograms through IR inspection windows. Delta-T > 15C above ambient or adjacent phase requires scheduled shutdown and busbar torque verification.

kbDocuments.title: BACnet/IP & Modbus TCP BMS Telemetry Timeout Playbook
kbDocuments.content: When Niagara N4 or Desigo PXC5 reports polling timeouts, ping gateway on VLAN 40, check RS-485 termination resistor (120 ohm), and inspect fiber SFP Rx optical power on NET-CORE-01.

kbDocuments.title: Service Scope Policy: Facility vs Personal Appliances
kbDocuments.content: FieldPilot engineering covers campus central HVAC, electrical distribution, life safety, and BMS infrastructure. Personal desk appliances (mini-fridges, coffee warmers, personal fans) are OUT_OF_SCOPE and should be redirected to Workplace Pantry / Employee IT Desk.
